prompt: On a map, $2$ inches represents $25$ miles. Two cities are $7.5$ inches apart on the map. What is the actual distance between the cities, in miles?
hint: Set up a proportion: inches over miles equals inches over miles.

hints.text: Set up a proportion: inches over miles equals inches over miles.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try a cleaner scale: $1$ inch to $10$ miles means $3$ inches is $30$ miles. Find what one inch represents, then multiply by the number of inches.

learningObjective: Apply a map scale that is not a unit rate.
explanation: Write the proportion with matching units in matching positions: $\dfrac{2 \text{ in}}{25 \text{ mi}} = \dfrac{7.5 \text{ in}}{d \text{ mi}}$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Convert to a per-inch rate
steps: $2$ inches is $25$ miles, so $1$ inch is $12.5$ miles.
Finding the per-one rate first makes the final step a single multiplication, and the intermediate value is easy to sanity-check.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: Multiplying 7.5 by 25 directly gives 187.5 — it forgets that 25 miles belongs to TWO inches, not one.
Reduce the scale to per-one-inch first (12.5 miles), or set the proportion with matching units stacked. Either habit blocks the doubling.
